justification: A uses a clean sans-serif with a navy cover, navy section bands and header/footer bars. The text is crisp and the banding is crisp. B's serif body is a bit less consistent and its green bands are fine but its text blocks are looser. B has a full-width image, a bit larger on B5, but A places the image under its own intro text, which gives a good page. B leaves the squares for missing glyphs in the permille signs on B6. A uses proper symbols. Both leave the same broken placeholder text on the history page.

A has a table of contents page and numbered headings in a clear hierarchy, with a lighter Arabic text face and tidy page flow. B skips the contents page and uses heavy navy banner headings, which suit a document with so few sections less well. B's tighter text blocks look dense, and its missing-glyph boxes appear on B3. The A contents page is mostly empty, which costs it some whitespace. The photo is handled about equally well in both (A5, B5).

B uses bold green banner bands behind section headings (B3, B4), and it adds running headers and footers with page numbers on every page. Its larger text is more readable and the body text fills the page more evenly. A has weak headings, thin rules and small dense text. A's page 2 is cramped, with its title page spare and its heading on page 6 barely distinct. The images are comparable on both.

Design A has a calmer layout. Its generous line spacing, clear section headings with rules, and a photo with a caption at the top of A6 give better reading comfort. Its section starts are cleanly separated. Design B adds a table of contents on B2, but that page is mostly empty. B also has heavy header and footer bands, and its dense text blocks have tighter spacing. Its photo sits mid-page after a text fragment carried over from the previous page, so the page rhythm feels more choppy. A's main weakness is that it has no table of contents.

A sets section headings in filled navy banners (A3, A5), which gives a clearer hierarchy than B's plain bold headings (B3, B5). A's sans body is tidy, and its image sits at the top of a page with a centred caption (A5). Both share the same broken Z-scheme markdown text on the last page (A6, B6), though A's page is entirely empty apart from that line. B's serif body is dense, and its image is squeezed between paragraphs (B5).

A uses navy header and footer bands and filled section banners ('Overview', 'Photosynthetic membranes and organelles') that make the structure easy to scan (A3, A5). B's serif body is elegant, but its headings are plain, small and nearly the same weight as the text, and it has only a thin top rule, so hierarchy is weaker (B3, B5). Both share the same flaws: broken equations and a raw markdown image link on the last page (A4, A6, B4, B6). A's running heads and page numbers help navigation, and its bold cover title is stronger.

B's dense serif text is easy to read, and its running headers, green section bands (B3, B4) and the manuscript image with caption (B7) give it a document structure and a real figure. A has a good sans typeface and a clever TOC divider (A4), but it has several mostly empty pages (A3, A4), only one tiny stray text line where an image should be (A5) and no real image at all. Its pages feel uneven, with large gaps. B's tight leading is slightly heavy and page 6 is half empty, which is why B wins only narrowly.

B has green section bands that give clear headings (B2, B3, B5), running headers and footers, and a larger, more legible Arabic font. Its text is evenly paced and the photo sits well between text blocks (B5). A has thin-rule headings that are weak, a smaller and denser font, and a photo that sits alone at the top of A5. A6 ends with a large empty area. The tiny uneven blue accent on the A cover is also weaker than B's cover.

A uses full-width green section bands with white headings, running headers and footers, and a cover with clear title hierarchy. Its image sits at full text width after the text. B has only thin rules and small right-aligned headings, so the hierarchy is weaker. Its text is dense and tightly set, and sections run on without separation. B's image sits at the top of page 5 and its last page is half empty. A's body text is more legible.

Design B has bold navy section bands with white headings, a running header and footer, and a larger image that flows with the text. Pages are filled consistently and body text is legible with clear hierarchy (B2, B3, B5). Design A has thin-rule headings, a small image on a mostly empty page, a half-empty page 6, and denser, smaller text. Its Latin and Arabic mixing in the title block is also less clean (A2, A5, A6).

A uses green full-width section bands (A3, A4) with white headings, clear running headers and footers, and well-spaced paragraphs, so the sections are easy to find. B has thin rules and small headings (B3, B4), and its Arabic text on B2 and B5 looks denser and more cramped. B also has no running header. Both covers are similar (A1, B1), and both place the manuscript image the same way (A7, B7).

A has a serif body with a sans heading, numbered headings, and a section-opener page (A3) with a sidebar band that gives clear hierarchy and structure. Its running headers show the subsection. Weaknesses: A3 is mostly empty, and A2 and A7 leave a lot of space. B is a plain flow of text with weak heading differentiation: the 'Characteristics' heading is a light weight, the others are bold, and the map on B6 sits alone on a mostly blank page. B is consistent and dense, but less distinctive and less hierarchical.

Both designs share one structure: a dark cover, running headers, section bands and a single photo. B's sans-serif body is cleaner and its tracking is consistent, but its text is cramped and the image page sits close to its text. A sets paragraphs apart more clearly, with spacing between them. Its green bands are bolder, and the photo with caption has more breathing room (A5). B justifies its text more tightly with uneven word gaps, and its page 3 text runs to the very bottom (B3). A's serif-like Arabic face reads well in a long document, and its page footers are lighter and cleaner. On balance A feels more refined and readable, though B's typography is crisp and modern. I lean slightly toward A.

A has a dark navy cover, header and footer bands with page numbers, a table of contents page, and bold numbered headings (A2, A4, A5). B's headings are small and weak, its pages are plain with no bands, and its text is dense, with some pages left half empty (B6). B's lighter text is slightly more compact. A's image page (A8) matches B's (B7), but A's banding frames it better.

A has a clear header and footer band with the running title and page numbers, numbered section headings, and a table of contents (A2). Its cover is a richer navy, and the image sits well between the text and the section heading (A6). B is clean and readable, with larger body text and a thin top rule. But it has no table of contents, its headings are less prominent, and page 3 ends with a large empty space. A is denser, with a sparse contents page and smaller text, but its structure and navigation are clearly stronger.

A uses full-width green heading bands, running headers with section names, and a well-placed photo with caption, giving clear hierarchy and rhythm (A2, A5). B's headings are thin rules with plain text, and its page 3 and 4 body text is large and spread out with uneven spacing. B's body text is loose and its first-page heading is barely different from the text (B2, B3). A's text is denser but cleaner. A's cover is a green slab similar to B's, so the cover does not separate them.

A uses navy header and footer bands with running titles and page numbers, which give it a clear structure, and its sans body reads cleanly with a clear H1/H2 distinction (A2, A3). Its flaw is big empty areas on A5 and A6, where the map sits alone at the top of an otherwise blank page. B has a serif body that reads well and fills its pages more evenly, but it has no bands, only plain footers. Its headings are inconsistent, since the Characteristics heading is bold and the intro line is large. B4 and B5 also have awkward gaps, with half a page empty after the figure and a large blank space above the rule on B5.

B has navy header and footer bands, a table of contents, numbered bold section headings, and a consistent running header on every page. Its body text is larger and easier to read. A has no TOC, and its first text page runs dense with no heading and a tiny font. Its headings are small and weak, and its page 6 is mostly empty. A also lacks bands and has a thin header rule only on some pages. B does leave the TOC page mostly empty and has an awkward stray image-path line on B5, but it is still more polished overall.

A uses navy header and footer bands and filled section banners (A3, A5), so sections stand out clearly. The map sits at the top of A5 with its caption, and the body text is a clean sans. A6 is nearly empty apart from a broken image markdown string. B has a serif face with odd letterspacing, and its headings are weaker. B also shows the same broken image string (B6), but within a fuller page. B's text flows continuously, which helps rhythm, but section starts sit awkwardly low and leave empty space on B5 and B6.

B has a contents page, running header and footer bands with page numbers, and clear numbered headings (1 حياته, 2 إسهاماته, 2.1). It also includes the manuscript image with a caption on B8. Text flows continuously, with no near-empty pages. A has a mostly empty page A3 and a divider page A4 with a clumsy sidebar, and its body pages lack heading structure. A's justified text shows uneven word spacing. Both designs show the same raw image-link text, so that does not separate them.

B's Arabic text is set in a clean serif with comfortable line spacing, and full-width green section bands make the headings obvious (B2, B3, B5). However, A looks more polished overall: its running header and footer bands, TOC page and caption layout give it a better structure (A2, A3, A6). B's text has missing-glyph boxes (B3, B6). A's body text is dense, though, and A2 is a mostly empty TOC page. On balance B is a close call and I give it a slight edge. The criteria scores lean toward A, which conflicts with this choice, and I am unsure.

A uses a clean modern Arabic sans with larger, clearer text and generous leading, so it reads comfortably (A2, A6). Its headings are clear and the dark cover is strong (A1). The top band and running footer are consistent. B uses a small, dense serif Arabic with tight leading, and the section headings are weak (B2, B3). Page B6 is mostly empty, which leaves the layout unbalanced. Both place the same photo similarly (A6, B5).

A uses a serif body with a larger lead paragraph and numbered headings, which gives a classic, readable text page. Its image sits mid-page, and the broken image markdown on A6 is shorter. B's sans body is light and tight, but its filled heading bands add structure. B also leaves a large gap on B4 and an unattached image at the top of B5. Both designs show the same broken Z scheme markdown on the last page.

A gives each section a navy heading band, a running header and footer bar with page numbers, and a darker cover. This makes the structure clear and consistent (A2, A3, A5). The image sits under the intro text with a caption, and body text is larger and easier to read. B has thin rules and small plain headings, so its hierarchy is weaker. Its text blocks look dense and gray, and its page 6 is half empty (B6). A does show a stray placeholder text line and glyph artifacts on A3, but B has the same artifacts on B3.

A has green section bands on A3 and A4, running headers and footers, and the manuscript image on A7, which together give clear hierarchy and a finished look. Its body text flows continuously across pages A2 to A6. B leaves page B3 mostly empty and spends B4 on a half-empty divider page with a dark side panel. B also drops the manuscript image and uses thin section headings (B6). B's typeface is cleaner and its text is tidy, but the layout is weaker and wastes space.

B has a cleaner Arabic text face, section headings and a running footer that names the section, and it includes the manuscript image with a caption (B7). A has a strong navy cover and a banded divider (A1, A4), but its body pages are dense and justified with uneven word spacing. A also has a mostly empty page 3 (A3) and no image. Both leave a stray image-path artifact in the text. B's pages have some blank areas (B6, B7), but B reads more consistently.

A has a clear sans-serif hierarchy and a rule-separated Characteristics section. Its content is packed in a steady page flow (A2-A4), with only a sparse final page (A6). B breaks the flow with a mostly empty page 2 (B2) and a divider page holding one short paragraph (B3). Its bullet list is split across pages (B3-B4), and its heading style is inconsistent, with a light h1 against bold subheads. B's divider sidebar is a distinctive touch, but it wastes space. B's serif body reads well, and its map sits better beside text (B7). Overall A is more cohesive and economical.

B reads better as a document. It has a table of contents on B2, numbered headings, and header and footer bands with page counts. Text runs continuously with a consistent rhythm. Its cover is navy with a blue rule. A has full-width green section bands (A2, A3) that give strong hierarchy. A's body text is denser, its pages break unevenly (A5 ends part-empty), and it has no contents page. B's only real weakness is the near-empty contents page (B2). A's imagery is slightly better, with a clearer caption block.

B has solid navy header bands behind section titles (B2, B3, B5) and header and footer bars with running titles and page numbers. This gives clear navigation and structure. B's text is denser and its page margins are tighter, but the pages feel consistent. B's image is larger and sits well in the text flow (B5). A's pages are airy with thin rules and larger text, but it has uneven page fills: A5 is half empty and A3 has a ragged ending. A's section headings are weaker, and the image page A6 reads well but lacks structure. B's cover is a brighter blue with a stronger accent line.

A uses a bold sans heading for 'Overview' and a larger lead paragraph, giving clearer hierarchy and a brighter cover. Its headings are slightly misaligned with the body indent, and page 5 has a large empty gap under the figure. B is cleaner and more consistent, with a top rule band and an even text block, but its headings are light and weak. B's page 6 is almost entirely empty apart from a broken image markdown line, which looks worse than A6, where the same broken line sits under a heading and text.

B reads better. Its larger, looser type and the thin top rule on each page give clearer, more comfortable lines (B2, B4). A packs smaller, denser text, so its pages feel crowded and the last page ends half empty (A2, A6). B's cover is a dark navy panel with a clean title, and A's is a flatter mid-blue; both are similar. B's headings are bigger and stand out more from the body, and the photo page balances better (B6 vs A5). B's pagination leaves some short pages, though (B3).

B's solid green section bands (Ismu, Tarikh, Ilm al-Muhitat) mark section changes clearly, and its running headers show the chapter name. The text is compact and the photo is larger and sits better with its caption. A has a clean navy cover and larger body text, but its headings are thin, with a hairline rule only. It also has a page 5 with a large empty lower area, and a half-empty photo page, so its pacing is uneven. A is more airy, but B reads as more structured.

A uses a serif body with generous margins and leading, a lead paragraph set larger than the body, and understated section headings with a thin rule. That reads as an editorial document (A2, A3, A5). B's sans body is dense and heavy, and its full-width navy header and footer bands plus filled heading blocks feel heavy and crowd the text (B2, B3, B5). Both share the same flaws: a broken image link on the last page and missing equation symbols (A6, B6, A4, B4). B's running headers do aid navigation, but A is more pleasant to read overall.

B has larger, airier Arabic text, a consistent top rule on every page and a bold section-divider page (B4). A uses a smaller, denser body with no strong section hierarchy, and its page 7 holds a lone manuscript image on an otherwise empty page, though that image is the one real asset. B's body pages are also left half-empty (B3), and the placeholder image text appears in both. Overall B looks more designed and more readable.

A has a TOC page, bold numbered headings (A4, A5) and consistent navy header and footer bands. Its body text is slightly larger with comfortable line spacing (A3). B has no TOC, and its section headings sit in green bands that look heavy (B3, B4). B's text is dense and its pages run on without clear breaks (B2). A's TOC is sparse and its page numbers are separated from the entries, which is a flaw. Both designs share the same image page.

B has a table of contents, running header and footer bands, numbered headings, and a clean sans-serif with consistent spacing (B2, B3, B6). Its headings sit clearly above the body text, and its photo is placed in the text flow with a caption (B6). A is more bare. Its pages have no header band, the page 6 text ends with a large empty space (A6), and the heading hierarchy is weaker. A's text is also denser, with more cramped lines and a leftover broken image link (A3). B has the same broken-link text (B4), so that does not separate them.

A uses a refined serif with consistent margins. Its headings sit at a clear level, and the map is placed with its caption at the top of A5, so the page is well composed. Its flaw is a nearly empty page A6 holding only a broken image markdown line. B's headings are bold sans pushed out to the left margin while the body is indented, which looks misaligned. B's justified text has loose letter-spacing, and its large blank areas on B5 and B6 also show the broken markdown image line. A's cover is darker and more elegant than B's flat blue cover.

A sets its section headings (الاسم, تاريخ البحر الأحمر, في علم المحيطات) in full-width navy bands (A2, A3, A5), which gives clear hierarchy and a steady rhythm. B uses plain bold headings with numbering (B3, B4), which are weaker. B adds a table of contents (B2), but that page is mostly empty and the page numbers sit oddly on the opposite side from their entries. A's photo has more breathing room with its text above (A5). B's photo sits directly under a text spillover from the previous page (B6). Both covers are nearly identical. Body text is dense in both; B's is slightly looser, and A's page 6 has a long unbroken block.

A has a stronger structure: header and footer bands with running titles, and a chapter-opener page (A3) with a navy sidebar and a large numbered title. Numbered subheads (1.1, 1.2) and the serif body make the hierarchy clear. Its weaknesses are the mostly empty pages A2 and A3 and the large blank area on A7. B is clean and consistent, with sans headings and a lighter footer, but it is flatter. B's headings are less differentiated, the body text is more cramped, and the chapter breaks are just a rule. Its blank space after the figure on B4 is also awkward.

A pairs a serif body with an elegant serif heading and a rule above the section headings. Its generous margins and leading give a refined, airy feel (A2, A3, A5). The image sits at the top of its own page with a clean caption (A5). Its thin top rule is subtler than B's heavy header and footer bands. The stray image-markdown text on A6 leaves a mostly empty page, but B has the same flaw (B6). B's bold sans headings clash somewhat with its serif body. B's dark header and footer bands add clutter, and its text is dense and tighter. B does flow continuously, with fewer mostly blank pages, and its running headers help navigation (B3, B5).

B runs continuously with consistent header and footer bands, numbered headings and a larger image that sits inside the text flow. A has a large empty gap on page 5 after the figure and a mostly blank page 6. Its headings are indented unevenly against the margins, and its letterspaced justified text creates loose lines. Both show the same raw markdown image text on the last page, so that flaw does not separate them.

A has navy header and footer bands carrying running titles and 'Page x of 6', and numbered section headings that make it feel structured. Its text flows continuously, with only a broken image placeholder leaving the last page mostly empty (A6). B has no bands, and its headings are outdented against indented body text, which looks misaligned (B3, B6). B also leaves a large gap on page 5 and puts a heading at the top of page 6 with a rule above it. Both show the same broken Z scheme image placeholder.

A runs continuously, with a clear sans heading hierarchy, an intro lead-in, and a bulleted list kept together on A2. B wastes pages: B2 is half empty, and the divider B3 leaves its intro sentence stranded from its bullets, which start on B4. B's header and footer bands and sidebar divider are bold, but they add heavy chrome and break the flow. B's body text is larger and fills the page more densely. A's images are slightly smaller but are placed well.

A has a table of contents, running header and footer bands with page numbers, bold numbered section headings, and the manuscript image on A8. B drops the image, has no TOC and no visible section headings inside the body text, and leaves page B3 mostly empty. B's divider page (B4) is stylish but half-empty, and its pages are plain walls of text. A's body text is dense but its headings give it clear structure.

A has bold sans section headings (A3 '1 Overview', A5 '2 Photosynthetic membranes...') that stand out, and header and footer bands that carry section names and page counts. B's headings are light and small, so the hierarchy is weaker. A places the figure inline mid-text with a caption (A5). B puts it at the top of its page, and B's page 3 ends mid-sentence. Both have the same broken image markdown at the end, but A's page 6 at least has running text above it, while B's page 6 is almost empty.

A pairs a geometric sans for headings with a serif body, and has clear heading levels, an indented text column and generous leading (A2, A3). Its figures sit with their related text, though A4 and A6 leave large empty areas below them. B's solid header and footer bands are heavy and repetitive, and its headings are weaker, with a thin-weight section title next to bold subheads (B2, B3). B also leaves the map alone on a mostly blank last page (B6) and has a large gap on B5. A's body text is more comfortable to read.

A uses full-width green section bands (A3, A4) that give clear section breaks, and its serif body is comfortable. But it has no contents page and its text is dense with a ragged mid-paragraph flow. B has a contents page (B2) and consistent navy header and footer bars with page counts. Its sans body is clean and its bold numbered headings (B4, B5, B7) are clear. B's headings are smaller, and its contents page is mostly empty with page numbers detached from entries. Overall B is more consistent and navigable.

A uses navy section banners with white headings, a header and footer band on every page, and a captioned image placed within the text flow (A5). Its text columns are full and consistent. B has thin rules and plain headings, so its hierarchy is weaker. B also leaves pages part empty (B3, B5) and has a header line without a footer band. B's inconsistent body sizes (large text on B6, smaller on B7) hurt its rhythm. A's header and footer text is small, but overall A reads as more structured and polished.

A has a darker cover, a header and footer band with running titles and page numbers, and a contents page. Its numbered, bold headings (A3, A4) give clearer hierarchy, and the sans-serif body reads cleanly. Its image is placed mid-page with a caption between text blocks (A6). B has no bands, and its serif text is denser with thin rules. B's headings are weaker, and the last page (B6) is half empty. A's contents page is mostly empty, and its rendering glitches are minor.

B uses filled navy section bands and running header and footer bands, which give clear navigation and hierarchy. Its image sits at full width, directly above the caption and the section it belongs to. Body text is compact and consistent. A has a serif body with inconsistent sizing: a large lead paragraph, then smaller justified text with wide letterspacing. Its headings are thin and mispositioned, indented differently from the body text. Page 5 of A is half empty after the image, and page 6 is mostly blank with a broken image markdown line. B also shows the broken markdown on its last page, which is nearly empty, but its bands make the document feel more finished overall.
